chunks: From him, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who was killed, then carried to the governor, and some people came and testified against a man that he had killed him intentionally. So the governor handed the killer over to the heirs of the slain so that retaliation might be carried out against him. But before they proceeded, a man came to them and confessed before the governor that he had intentionally killed their companion, and that this one against whom the witnesses had testified was innocent of killing your companion. So do not kill him, and take me for his blood.

He said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “If the heirs of the slain wish to kill the one who confessed against himself, then let them kill him, and they have no claim against the other. And the heirs of the one who confessed against himself have no claim against the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given. But if they wish to kill the one against whom testimony was given, then let them kill him, and they have no claim against the one who confessed. Then the one who confessed against himself must pay half of the blood money to the one against whom testimony was given.”

I said: What if they wish to kill both of them together? He said: “That is for them, but they must pay half of the blood money specifically to the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given, not to the other man’s heirs; then they may kill them both for him.”
I said: What if they wish to take the blood money? He said: “The blood money is divided equally between the two, because one of them confessed and against the other testimony was given.”

I said: Then how was half of the blood money made due from the one who confessed to the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given when he was killed, while nothing was made due to the heirs of the one who confessed against the heirs of the one against whom testimony was given and who did not confess? He said: “Because the one against whom testimony was given is not like the one who confessed. The one against whom testimony was given did not confess and did not absolve his companion, while the other confessed and absolved his companion. So what became binding upon the one who confessed and absolved his companion did not become binding upon the one against whom testimony was given, who did not confess and did not absolve his companion.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.بَرِيءٌ: declared innocent and free of the killing
key_terms.شُهِدَ عَلَيْهِ: witness testimony was given against him
key_terms.لِيُقَادَ بِهِ: for qiṣāṣ to be carried out against him
key_terms.نِصْفَ ٱلدِّيَةِ: half of the prescribed blood money
key_terms.ٱلْوَالِي: the governing authority or ruler handling the criminal case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one man is accused of murder by witnesses and another later confesses to the killing?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for a murder case in which one person is convicted by witness testimony and another later confesses to the killing. It explains the options of the victim’s heirs regarding qiṣāṣ or diyah, and clarifies how liability is apportioned between confession and testimony. The ruling distinguishes between the one who merely had testimony against him and the one who confessed and thereby exonerated the other.
